questions.text: Learning that someone has had bad news usually makes me want to reach out.
I routinely say no to requests that don't align with my personal objectives.
I feel the emotional atmosphere of a room the moment I walk in, and it lands in my body immediately.
I value variety in my daily routine because it keeps me mentally sharp and engaged.
I routinely translate, explain, or simplify information so others can access it.
I pick up on the way someone's posture shifts when a particular person enters the room.
Hearing that a problem harms many people rarely makes me want their suffering reduced.
I act on my initial understanding and ask for clarification only if I get stuck.
I feel that when I take care of my own needs, I am better equipped for everything else.
I prefer to speak off the cuff because rehearsed delivery feels stiff to me.
I don't see other people's private suffering as something I need to be concerned about.
When I am near someone in deep pain, their suffering exists in my awareness as a moral weight that requires a response.
I do not usually register when a person responds with slightly more distance after I said something they disagreed with.
I find it difficult to tell whether a group's silence indicates contentment or suppressed disagreement.
I do not usually notice when a text message carries emotional subtext that goes beyond the words.
Another person's serious suffering weighs on me.
I notice that I can sit with ambiguity and uncertainty without my nervous system escalating.
I keep a record of decisions and the reasoning behind them for future reference.
I review my calendar at the start of each day to set my intentions.
I routinely choose the option that benefits others, even when a different choice would benefit me more.
I routinely audit my commitments and drop those that no longer serve my personal direction.
I tend to view emotional intensity in others with a kind of curiosity because my own experience is different.
I would choose a less prestigious school or job if the alternative let me stay close to people who need me.
Even a mildly critical tone of voice can set off alarm bells throughout my system.
I have a tendency to take over tasks that others are doing too slowly.
I can tell when a person adjusts their level of formality mid-conversation in response to a social cue they received.
I notice that I can move from a difficult situation to a normal one without needing a transition period.
When entering a new group, I observe how things work before settling into a role.
I go from calm to fully activated in a matter of seconds.
I tend to consult the team before making any scope changes mid-project.
Wanting someone else's suffering to ease is rarely part of how I respond to their situation.
I tend to be the one who says the meeting is over and assigns next steps.
I sense when the energy of a room drops the moment a particular person starts speaking.
I practice new skills in a structured, progressive way, building from simple to complex.
I naturally listen first and speak after others have shared their thoughts.
I think of authority as something to be exercised, not just held.
